title: A summary cloze on the causal links
statement: Put a summary gap-fill's blanks on the causal links that hold the whole text together, never on incidental details or connecting words.
example: The specification sets exactly four blanks, and the course gives them a bank of six words.
detail: The curriculum's lesson-component specification makes the summary a compressed, causal retell with exactly four blanks on the links in the student's mental model, so that it checks the student followed the flow of the story, not incidental detail, and uses wrong words that were true earlier but not now to test that the student tracked the change (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/inputs/procedures/Example_Lesson_Components.txt`, line 20). The course's criteria register adds a bank of six words, answers true to the text and no blank on a connecting word, checked by a person (`grade3-reading/artifacts/criteria-register.csv`, line 26).
against: The whole-text rule was not applied consistently: six of the nine science designs still certify the old untouched-section gap-fill in their closing line, for example `downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.2 - The Living World - Lesson Designs/3.2 - 9. The Invisible World Microorganisms - FIND - Lesson Design (v2 - MCQ pauses + science sweep).docx`, line 195.

evidence.quote: so it checks that the child has followed the flow of the story, not incidental detail
“true-earlier-but-not-now” distractors test that the child tracked how things changed
exactly four blanks on the links of the mental model, bank of 6, answers text-true, no connective blank
